identity.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
alt_names: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis

land.text: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla, the three islands of the associated state

predecessors.note: The islands were British colonies (English settlement from 1623, British since the 1713 and 1783 treaties on the Saint Kitts and Nevis page); in 1967 they became an associated state with full internal autonomy, the UK keeping external affairs and defence.

capitals.name: Basseterre
capitals.note: 'The capital city is Basseterre, located on the larger island of Saint Kitts.'

correction.text: the two islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis in the Leeward Islands, 261 km2, capital Basseterre (the associated state also held Anguilla from February to May 1967, see the ledger)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 501 km2 polygon (64.89-64.58 W, 17.64-17.84 N) lies on Saint Croix in the US Virgin Islands, not on Saint Kitts (62.7 W). Infobox area 261 km2 against 501 km2 is a ratio of 1.9 and the place is wrong in any case; the polygon must not be used for 1967-2023. At the grid's 253 km2 cell the true state is one cell (Anguilla another).

correction.text: the two islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis, 261 km2

keyframe_review.note: Same Saint Croix polygon as 1967-2023; replace it with the country.

region.text: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla, the three islands of the associated state

ledger.note: 27 February 1967: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla becomes an associated state of the United Kingdom. The page's table lists 'Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla: 27 February 1967'; the Saint Kitts and Nevis page says 'the islands became an associated state with full internal autonomy in 1967.'

region.text: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla, the three islands of the associated state

ledger.note: 27 February 1967: the UK keeps external affairs and defence. 'Under the act each state had full control over its constitution (and thus internal self-government)' and 'the UK retained responsibility for external affairs and defence'; shown as a client relation until independence. The mapping of 'associated state' to a vassal tint is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Anguilla, which 'chose to secede from the union in 1967'

ledger.note: 30 May 1967: Anguilla ejects the St Kitts police and leaves the union. 'On 30 May 1967, Anguillans forcibly ejected the St Kitts police force from the island'; the Anguilla page's infobox dates the secession and declaration of independence to 12 July 1967, the Saint Kitts and Nevis page says 'Anguilla chose to secede from the union in 1967' and the West Indies Associated States page says 1969. Anguilla is a de facto loss from this date.

region.text: Anguilla, formally separated in 1980 and 'a British overseas territory'

ledger.note: December 1980: Anguilla's separation from Saint Kitts and Nevis is made formal. Infobox 'Formal secession from Saint Kitts and Nevis: 16 December 1980'; the Saint Kitts and Nevis page says 'In 1971 Britain resumed full control of Anguilla, but it was formally separated in 1980' and the West Indies Associated States footnote gives 29 October 1980; British troops had restored control on 18 March 1969. The land was already out of the state's hands since 1967; this closes the de jure tie.

region.text: the two islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis

ledger.note: 19 September 1983: the UK's responsibility for external affairs and defence ends with full independence. 'St Kitts and Nevis achieved full independence on 19 September 1983.'

19 September 1983: Saint Kitts and Nevis becomes fully independent as the Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis ('Today, the Constitution refers to the state as both Saint Kitts and Nevis and Saint Christopher and Nevis'); same state, same land.

wars.name: Anguilla crisis (secession of Anguilla)
wars.outcome: Anguilla stayed out of the union: '300 British troops were sent to the island' in March 1969, British authority was 'confirmed by the Anguilla Act 1971 (c. 63) of July 1971' and Anguilla was formally separated in 1980.
wars.note: The land change is carried by the two loss events (1967 de facto, 1980 de jure), so the zone is left empty; the page gives no fighting beyond the 30 May 1967 ejection of the police.

certainty.note: Island coasts; Anguilla's status is the exception for 1967-1980 (outside the state in fact from 1967, formally until 1980).

notes: Cliopatria's 'Saint Kitts' (1967..2024) is a 501 km2 polygon on Saint Croix, so both shapes are 'wrong' and the true state is {'country': 'Saint Kitts and Nevis'}. The Wikipedia field 'Saint Kitts' (and Wikidata Q204989) are the island's; the state's own article is 'Saint Kitts and Nevis' (used here for every fact). Start 1967 follows Cliopatria's first year and the associated-state date (the sibling dossier antigua-and-barbuda does the same). Disagreement on Anguilla: the Anguilla page dates its leaving to 30 May / 12 July 1967 and its formal separation to 16 December 1980; the West Indies Associated States page says 1969 and 29 October 1980. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape holds no cell of Saint Kitts and Nevis or Anguilla in 1966 (checked with the gazetteer), so the associated-state birth has no matching loss in that row. Anguilla (British since March 1969) needs a short dossier of its own (counterpart 'Anguilla', suggested slug anguilla). The 1998 Nevis referendum on separation 'fell short of the required two-thirds majority' (Saint Kitts and Nevis page), so no territorial event. The page budget (1-2) was exceeded by one page (three opened) because the associated-state date needed the third.
